title: The Diffusion Duality, Chapter II: $\Psi$-Samplers and Efficient Curriculum
claim: Our corrector-based sampler keeps improving as sampling steps increase, while ancestral baselines plateau, beating strong baselines across modalities.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared NFE x-axis, per-point entropy annotations
description: Two side-by-side line charts share a log-style NFE x-axis running from 32 to 4096. The left plot shows generative perplexity (lower is better) on language modeling. The right plot shows FID (lower is better) on CIFAR-10. Each plot has four curves: MDLM and Duo++ as faint dashed lines, and MDLM+ReMDM and Duo++ with the Ψ-sampler as solid, saturated lines. Red marks the MDLM family and blue marks the Duo family. The dashed baselines flatten at higher NFEs. The solid Ψ-sampler curve in blue keeps dropping and ends lowest. In the left plot, small parenthesized unigram-entropy numbers sit beside the points. A legend sits in the top right of each plot. The eye goes first to the steep blue solid line.
caption: Performance on Language Modeling and Image Modeling. \psisamplers{} generalize ReMDM [ref] to arbitrary noise distributions. (Left): Generative perplexity (Gen.\ PPL; $\downarrow$) as a function of NFEs, with nucleus sampling $p=0.9$. \psisamplers{} consistently improve with more steps, unlike ancestral sampling which plateaus. Curves are annotated with the average unigram entropy per sequence as a proxy for diversity. (Right): On CIFAR-10, \psisamplers{} achieve better FID ($\downarrow$) than MDLM (with ReMDM).
abstract: Uniform-state discrete diffusion models excel at few-step generation and guidance due to their ability to self-correct, making them preferred over autoregressive or Masked diffusion models in these settings. However, their sampling quality plateaus with ancestral samplers as the number of steps increases. We introduce a family of Predictor-Corrector (PC) samplers for discrete diffusion that generalize prior methods and apply to arbitrary noise processes. When paired with uniform-state diffusion, our samplers outperform ancestral sampling on both language and image modeling, achieving lower generative perplexity at matched unigram entropy on OpenWebText and better FID/IS scores on CIFAR10. Crucially, unlike conventional samplers, our PC methods continue to improve with more sampling steps. Taken together, these findings call into question the assumption that Masked diffusion is the inevitable future of diffusion-based language modeling. Beyond sampling, we develop a memory-efficient curriculum for the Gaussian relaxation training phase, reducing training time by 25% and memory by 33% compared to Duo while maintaining comparable perplexity on OpenWebText and LM1B and strong downstream performance. We release code, checkpoints, and a video-tutorial on https://s-sahoo.github.io/duo-ch2/
